name: Comet Quantum RNG Engine
description: Random bytes from Born-rule measurements on IBM hardware (or Aer baseline), with an SP 800-90B min-entropy certificate, Toeplitz extractor and CHSH witness.

integers.description: Uniform integers in [min, max] via rejection sampling.

backend_name.description: IBM backend to target; omit to auto-select the least busy device. Ignored when mode='emu'.
backend_name.title: Backend Name

bell_witness.description: Add 8 qubits carrying four CHSH Bell pairs measured in the same job (fidelity witness).
bell_witness.title: Bell Witness

derive.description: Optional unbiased integers/floats derived from the conditioned bytes.

epsilon_log2.description: Extractor security parameter: output is 2^-epsilon_log2-close to uniform.
epsilon_log2.title: Epsilon Log2

include_raw_counts.description: Echo the raw counts so third parties can recompute the output.
include_raw_counts.title: Include Raw Counts

mode.description: 'emu' samples on a local Aer simulator (classical baseline, uncertified); 'qpu' samples IBM hardware.
mode.title: Mode

num_qubits.description: Width of the randomness register (Born-rule bits per shot).
num_qubits.title: Num Qubits

output_bytes.description: Conditioned bytes requested. You receive min(output_bytes, extractable).
output_bytes.title: Output Bytes

prev_pulse_hash.description: Previous beacon pulse hash to chain onto (hex).
prev_pulse_hash.title: Prev Pulse Hash

public_seed.description: Toeplitz seed: a shipped seed id (default 'toeplitz-v1', uniform seed from a documented ceremony — information-theoretic mode) or any custom string (SHAKE-256 expanded — computational mode, labelled as such).
public_seed.title: Public Seed

qpu_instance.description: IBM Quantum instance CRN; BYOK override, omit to use mothbackend's own shared IBM credentials.
qpu_instance.title: Qpu Instance

qpu_token.description: IBM Quantum API token; BYOK override, omit to use mothbackend's own shared IBM credentials.
qpu_token.title: Qpu Token

require_assumption_free.description: Certify only on the assumption-free tier (whole-shot most-common-value bound, no independence assumed). Capped near log2(shots) bits per shot; ≈0 in counts mode, so this effectively needs per-shot memory readout.
require_assumption_free.title: Require Assumption Free

shots.description: Number of measurement shots (max 10,000). Raw bits = num_qubits × shots.
shots.title: Shots

description_md:
Comet Quantum RNG Engine (comet-qrng-v1) — hardware Born-rule randomness with an honest certificate.

You ask for random bytes. The engine prepares `num_qubits` qubits in |+⟩, measures
them on a simulator (`emu`) or an IBM QPU (`qpu`) through mothbackend, estimates
how much min-entropy the device's output actually carried (NIST SP 800-90B
estimators on the real data — not an assumed constant), runs it through a
seeded Toeplitz extractor with a stated security parameter, and returns the
bytes together with everything needed to audit them.

## What you send

`application/json`:

```json
{"num_qubits": 12, "shots": 4096, "mode": "emu", "output_bytes": 32,
 "bell_witness": true, "derive": {"integers": {"min": 1, "max": 6, "count": 10}}}
```

- **`num_qubits`** — width of the randomness register (one Born-rule bit per
  qubit per shot). `emu` caps the whole circuit at 20 qubits; `qpu` is bounded
  by the backend.
- **`shots`** — repetitions (≤ 10,000). Raw bits = num_qubits × shots.
- **`bell_witness`** — add 8 qubits carrying four CHSH Bell pairs measured in the
  same job. Yields an S value that *can fail* on hardware (a fidelity witness,
  not device-independent certification — see `bell_witness.caveat`).
- **`output_bytes`** — how many conditioned bytes you want. You get
  `min(output_bytes, extractable)`; the certificate says which.
- **`derive`** — optional unbiased integers / floats derived from the bytes.
- **`prev_pulse_hash`, `pulse_index`** — chain this run as a beacon pulse.
- **`public_seed`, `epsilon_log2`** — extractor parameters (public; defaults fine).

## What you get back

`GET /result/{job_id}` → `result.output`:

```json
{
  "random": {"hex": "9f3a…", "bytes": 32, "derived": {"integers": {"values": [3, 6, 1, …]}}},
  "certificate": {"certified": true, "grade": "hardware", "h_bit": 0.91,
                  "budget_bits": 388211, "output_bits": 256, "epsilon_log2": 64, "statements": ["…"]},
  "entropy": {"readout": "counts", "h_bit": 0.91, "ordering_penalty_bits": 43250.8, "…": "…"},
  "bell_witness": {"S": 2.61, "sigma_S": 0.012, "violates_classical_3sigma": true, "…": "…"},
  "device_fingerprint": {"z_expectations": ["…"], "top_correlated_pairs": ["…"]},
  "provenance": {"mode": "qpu", "backend": "ibm_miami", "provider_job_id": "…", "qpu_seconds": 3.1, "circuit_hash": "…"},
  "commitment": {"commit": "…", "salt": "…", "committed_at": "…"},
  "pulse": {"pulse_hash": "…", "prev_hash": "…", "…": "…"},
  "raw": {"counts_sha256": "…", "counts": {"0110…": 1, "…": "…"}}
}
```

`emu` output is a classical simulator's pseudo-randomness. It is returned with
`certificate.certified = false, grade = "simulator-baseline"` — it is the
control the hardware result is compared against, not a product claim.

## Pipeline (internal)

  build   → Params → CircuitSpec → QASM bytes (+ circuit_hash)
  submit  → mothbackend.client: emu inline → counts; qpu → job id. Forms the
            commitment C = H(circuit_hash ‖ backend ‖ job_id ‖ salt) BEFORE any
            outcome exists and surfaces it via update_progress.
  collect → emu passthrough │ qpu: poll until terminal → counts (+ memory if the
            backend ever returns per-shot data), usage_seconds
  format  → entropy assessment → Toeplitz extraction → derivations → CHSH
            witness → device fingerprint → certificate → pulse

Bitstring convention: mothbackend reports counts qubit-0-LEFTMOST; everything
here consumes strings directly. Circuit qubits [0, num_qubits) are the
randomness register; the next 8 are the witness pairs.

code_samples.source:
import time, requests

BASE = "https://api.mothquantum.com/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY"}

r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/generation/comet-qrng-v1/process", headers=HEADERS,
                  json={"num_qubits": 12, "shots": 2048, "mode": "emu", "output_bytes": 32,
                        "derive": {"integers": {"min": 1, "max": 6, "count": 10}}})
job_id = r.json()["job_id"]
while True:
    s = requests.get(f"{BASE}/status/{job_id}", headers=HEADERS).json()
    if s["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(2)
out = requests.get(f"{BASE}/result/{job_id}", headers=HEADERS).json()["result"]["output"]
print(out["random"]["hex"], out["random"]["derived"]["integers"]["values"])
print(out["certificate"]["grade"], out["certificate"]["statements"])

import time, requests

BASE = "https://api.mothquantum.com/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY"}

r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/generation/comet-qrng-v1/process", headers=HEADERS,
                  json={"num_qubits": 100, "shots": 10000, "mode": "qpu",
                        "output_bytes": 4096, "bell_witness": True})
job_id = r.json()["job_id"]
while True:
    s = requests.get(f"{BASE}/status/{job_id}", headers=HEADERS).json()
    for step in s.get("steps", []):
        print(step["name"], "→", step["status"])   # the submit step surfaces the commitment
    if s["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(10)
out = requests.get(f"{BASE}/result/{job_id}", headers=HEADERS).json()["result"]["output"]
print(out["certificate"]["certified"], out["certificate"]["h_bit"], out["random"]["bytes"], "bytes")
print("CHSH S =", out["bell_witness"]["S"], "±", out["bell_witness"]["sigma_S"])
print("pulse", out["pulse"]["pulse_hash"])

error_codes.description: Parameter validation failed (e.g. circuit exceeds the EMU cap of 20 qubits).
The circuit needs more qubits than the selected IBM backend provides.
IBM authentication failed — no usable token/instance (shared or BYOK).
Could not retrieve the QPU result — job cancelled, failed, or backend errored.
The QPU job did not reach a terminal state within the engine's 6000 s poll deadline; the provider job was cancelled.
The backend returned counts that do not match the submitted circuit.
